originalTitle: Oil rally weighs on Indian bonds, value buyers limit fall
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: Indian government bonds have been losing value for four days in a row. This is largely because oil prices are rising, which is making people worried about India's economy. As a result, the interest rates on these bonds (called yields) have gone up to their highest point since late June. The Indian currency, the rupee, has also weakened against the US dollar, which isn't helping. However, some investors are still buying these bonds, which is limiting the extent of the decline in value.

originalTitle: IndusInd Bank Q1 Results: Profit soars 72% YoY to Rs 1,037 crore; NII flat
simplifiedContent: IndusInd Bank just released its quarterly results, and its profit increased by 72% compared to the same time last year, reaching Rs 1,037 crore. This happened even though the bank's income from interest on loans didn't change much and it earned less from fees. The bank's overall health improved, with better asset quality, more deposits, and stronger capital. However, the bank did have fewer loans, which is because it's focusing on making sure its loans are good quality rather than just increasing their number. This is a positive sign for the bank's stability and future growth.

originalTitle: Why Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger don't like EBITDA as an earnings metric
simplifiedContent: Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger, two well-known investors, don't think EBITDA is a good way to measure how well a company is doing. EBITDA is a way to calculate a company's earnings, but it leaves out some important costs, like depreciation. Buffett and Munger think this can make a company look healthier than it really is, which can be misleading for investors. They believe that ignoring these costs gives a false picture of a company's financial situation. This matters because investors use earnings metrics like EBITDA to decide whether to buy or sell a company's stock.

originalTitle: PSU stock Coal India sets board meeting date to declare final dividend for FY26, record date. Details here
simplifiedContent: Coal India, a big company that mines coal, is going to have a meeting to decide on paying a final dividend to its shareholders. The dividend is ₹5.25 per share, which means if you own shares of Coal India, you'll get this amount of money for each share you own. To be eligible for this dividend, you need to own the shares on or before September 4, 2026, which is called the record date. The company will release more details on how taxes will be handled for this dividend soon. This meeting is part of the company's annual general meeting, which will be held on August 31, 2026.

originalTitle: Expert view: Market recovery may be closer than most people think, says Monarch Networth Capital CEO
simplifiedContent: The CEO of Monarch Networth Capital, Gaurav Bhandari, has a positive view of the Indian stock market. He thinks that even though the market has been struggling lately, it might start to recover soon. This means that the market could start to do better and stock prices might go up. This is important because it could be a good time for investors to consider buying stocks. The CEO's opinion suggests that a recovery might happen sooner than many people expect.

originalTitle: IndusInd Bank Q1 Results 2026: Net profit surges 72% at  ₹1,037 crore, NII up just 1%
simplifiedContent: IndusInd Bank just released its financial results for the first quarter of 2026, and it's good news: the bank's profit increased by 72% compared to last year, reaching ₹1,037 crore. This means the bank made a lot more money than it did during the same time last year. The bank's Net Interest Income, which is the money it makes from lending, only increased by 1% to ₹4,685 crore. The bank was also able to reduce its operating expenses, which is the money it spends on running the bank, by 12.5%. This increase in profit is significant and shows that the bank is doing well financially.
